open_points.subject: Source-supplied timestamp representation
open_points.text: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes” conflicts with source-supplied times being “validated and kept as supplied” when a supplied datetime contains an offset or is not already represented as naive UTC.
open_points.question: Which source timestamp representations are accepted, and are accepted offset-aware values converted to naive UTC, rejected, or persisted with their supplied representation?
options: Require naive datetimes and interpret them as UTC
Require offset-aware datetimes, convert the instant to naive UTC, and discard the offset
Accept either form and normalize both to naive UTC
Keep an offset-aware supplied value unchanged despite the persisted-timestamp rule
open_points.default_guess: Accept offset-aware inputs, normalize their instants to UTC, and persist them without an offset.

witness.initial: No snapshot exists for the identity; the producer has valid import access.
events: The producer publishes a snapshot whose approved_at is 2026-08-09T12:00:00+02:00 and published_at is 2026-08-09T10:30:00Z.
outcomes: The import is accepted after both values are converted to naive UTC.
The import is rejected because supplied source timestamps must already be offset-naive UTC; alternatively, an implementation following “kept as supplied” persists the offsets.
witness.observer: The producer sees acceptance or rejection, and later readers can see different stored timestamp representations.

open_points.subject: Validation of source-supplied times
open_points.text: “Times a source supplies … are validated and kept as supplied” does not state what validation is performed beyond identifying them as source values.
open_points.question: Which temporal conditions make a supplied time invalid—for example a past or present credential expiry, approved_at after published_at, confirmed_at in the future, or future photo and payment dates?
options: Validate only datetime/date shape and the required UTC representation
Also require source-event ordering such as approved_at <= published_at
Also reject source event times unreasonably in the future
Require a service credential expires_at to be strictly after the operation instant
open_points.default_guess: Validate representation and declared field type only, except require a newly issued credential expiry to be later than the operation instant.

witness.initial: An administrator is active and may issue a service credential.
events: At 12:00 UTC the administrator requests a credential with expires_at equal to 11:59 UTC.
outcomes: The issue is refused because a newly issued credential must have a future expiry.
The credential is issued successfully but is unusable immediately under the strict expiry comparison.
witness.observer: The administrator sees refusal versus a successful one-time credential response.

open_points.subject: Boundary of a single clock-reading operation
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps … and every current-time comparison” does not define whether authentication, authorization, the owning use case, nested modules, and audit writing within one HTTP request are one operation or separate operations.
open_points.question: What is the clock-sharing boundary, and must the sampled instant be passed through authentication, authorization, and all nested use-case work for one request?
options: One HTTP command/request has one shared instant, except the audit writer’s occurred_at
Each public application use case has its own instant, so authentication and the invoked use case may sample separately
Each module invocation is an operation and may sample independently
open_points.default_guess: Use one shared instant for the complete application command, including authentication and authorization, with only audit_writer allowed its explicit second sample.

witness.initial: A staff session expires at 12:00:00; the request begins just before that instant and no other revocation applies.
events: Staff sends a project mutation at 11:59:59.999.
Authentication samples the time before expiry.
The owning mutation use case begins after 12:00:00.
outcomes: A request-wide instant is reused, so the session is valid and the mutation may commit.
Authentication and the use case are separate operations; the use case samples again, treats the session as expired, and refuses the mutation.
witness.observer: The staff caller sees mutation success versus authentication refusal.

open_points.subject: Timestamp precision and persistence canonicalization
open_points.text: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes” and “one instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp” do not define supported fractional precision or whether persistence rounds or truncates clock and source instants.
open_points.question: What timestamp precision is canonical in storage and comparisons, and must higher-precision values be rejected, rounded, or truncated?
options: Canonicalize all timestamps to whole seconds
Let each persistence adapter choose its precision
open_points.default_guess: Preserve microsecond precision and compare the exact persisted values.

witness.initial: A session has a persisted expiry of 12:00:00.500000 UTC.
events: A request is authorized at 12:00:00.250000 UTC.
outcomes: With microsecond precision, now < expires_at and the session is usable.
With whole-second truncation, both values become 12:00:00 and the strict boundary makes the session expired.
witness.observer: The session holder sees authorization success versus expiry refusal.
